slides.stem: If $a = 2.5(b + c)$ and $b$ is $40\%$ of $c$, then $a$ is what percent of $b$?

slides.intro: Plug a clean number into the smallest piece: let $c = 100$.
slides.trapWhy: $290\%$ tries to add $250\% + 40\%$. Stacked percents only behave through real numbers.

slides.title: Concrete numbers beat percent algebra
slides.body:
When percents chain across relationships, assign the smallest variable a clean value like $100$ and compute forward.

"$X$ is what percent of $Y$" is always $\frac{X}{Y} \times 100$ — with actual numbers, it's one division.
